text: Classical (conditional-analysis) compatibilism, associated with Hume, Moore, and Ayer, analyses 'S could have done otherwise' as which of the following?
choices: S's action was uncaused by any prior event.
There is a possible world with the same laws and the same past in which S does otherwise.
S would have done otherwise if S had chosen (or wanted) to do otherwise.
S has an agent-causal power to originate a new causal chain.
explanation: The conditional (hypothetical) analysis renders 'could have done otherwise' as a counterfactual about what S would have done given a different choice, which can be true even under determinism. 'Uncaused action' and 'agent-causal power' are libertarian, and the 'same laws and past' gloss is closer to Lewis's local-miracle reading than to the classical conditional analysis.
